page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile characterized by moderate multi-core capabilities paired with weaker single-core execution. The single-core performance is positioned in the bottom 25% tier, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 935.0 and a weak stress-ng single-core metric. Single-threaded gzip compression is particularly limited, falling into the bottom 10% category. Conversely, multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression and Geekbench multi-core tasks, achieve average performance tiers. Memory bandwidth tests also demonstrate average throughput, reaching 96.89 GB/sec for large block read-only operations.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.6xlarge offers a dense memory allocation relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The instance is suited for database operations, as reflected in its average Passmark database score and Redis SET throughput of 16.8 million operations per second. Other appropriate workloads include multi-threaded text processing, static web serving, and moderate software compilation tasks.
